claim: Harness-only changes moved a framework from rank 30 to top 5 on Terminal-Bench 2.0; benchmark scores can differ 20–30+ pp based on scaffold alone.
quote: Framework scaffolding can contribute 30+ percentage points. Different benchmarks reward different capabilities, so frontier labs typically report scores on at least three.

claim: Agent evaluation requires three levels — end-to-end, trajectory, and component — with 12 primary metrics across tool use, planning, output, and safety.
quote: An agent does much more than simply generate a response. Before it answers, it might make a plan, call tools, inspect tool outputs, revise its approach, maintain state, retry failed steps, or hand work off to another agent.

claim: pass@k measures whether a solution exists in k attempts; pass^k measures whether all k attempts succeed — the two diverge significantly above k=3.
quote: Two metrics address agent variability: pass@k: probability of success in at least one of k attempts; pass^k: probability that all k trials succeed.

claim: A five-step evaluation harness covers: define success criteria, create representative test cases, instrument with tracing, choose evaluation methods, run and analyze.
quote: Tracing captures every decision the agent makes during execution, including which tool it selected, what arguments it constructed, and what response it received.

claim: Terminal-Bench 2.0 is the benchmark where harness-only changes moved an agent from rank 30 to top 5 without model changes.
quote: Terminal Bench 2.0 — Referenced for ranking coding agents; harness-only changes moved an agent 'from rank 30 to top 5' without model changes.

claim: Production harness evaluation targets: tool accuracy >95%, task success rate >90%, loop rate 0%, with chaos engineering to test error recovery via injected failures.
quote: Chaos Engineering: Purposefully inject faults into the mocked environment...to test the agent's error recovery. This includes returning 500 errors and malformed JSON responses.

claim: Six dimensions any agent eval framework must score independently: tool selection accuracy, argument extraction, result utilization, error recovery, plan coherence, task completion.
quote: Aggregate 'did it work' tells you nothing about which layer regressed last Tuesday.

claim: Five demo modes exist for live AI demos: Verified Live, Constrained Live, Pre-flight Live, Pre-Recorded, and Aspirational; credibility breaks when mode is ambiguous.
quote: Credibility breaks when the presentation mode doesn't match audience expectations. The 2023 Gemini video controversy emerged because viewers couldn't tell if they were watching live or edited content.

claim: A production harness consists of 12 modules across orchestration, interaction, and persistence layers; Hashline improved code-editing success from 6.7% to 68.3% via harness-only changes.
quote: Hashline increased code-editing success rates from 6.7% to 68.3%, while reducing token consumption by 61%.

claim: SkillTester benchmarks agent skills across 86 tasks in 11 domains, finding that higher utility consistently correlates with increased security risk — score both independently.
quote: Higher utility often correlates with increased security risks when skills are designed with fewer restrictions or broader access permissions.

claim: AdaRubric generates task-adaptive evaluation rubrics rather than fixed criteria, improving inter-annotator agreement and reward model training quality.
quote: Task-adaptive evaluation criteria adjust based on the particular problem domain, improving alignment between evaluation metrics and actual task objectives.

claim: SkillFlow shows embedding-based retrieval substantially outperforms keyword matching for complex skill queries; Recall@K and MRR are the key metrics for skill-library navigability.
quote: Structured skill representation substantially improves agent task completion rates; embedding-based methods excel for complex skill queries.

claim: Six primary dimensions for comparing agent frameworks: architecture, state management, tool integration and MCP support, multi-agent orchestration, observability, production readiness.
quote: The agent framework wars of 2026 are not about which framework is 'best'...they are about which set of trade-offs aligns with the way your team builds software.

claim: A unified eval framework using instruction-tool-environment triplets shows up to 37.7% of apparent agent failures stem from environmental constraints (timeouts, anti-crawling), not model deficits.
quote: Environmental Volatility Separates from Agent Reasoning: Online-to-offline comparisons isolate environmental failures from model deficits. Offline gains reached +37.7% for some models.

claim: CrewAI deploys multi-agent teams 40% faster than LangGraph but adds approximately 18% token overhead; LangGraph and OpenAI Swarm lead in token efficiency.
quote: CrewAI enables deploying a multi-agent team 40% faster than LangGraph. LangGraph and OpenAI Swarm lead in token efficiency because they minimize redundant LLM calls.

claim: Berkeley researchers demonstrated reward-hacking of all major benchmarks by April 2026; third-party evaluation scores are more trustworthy than self-reported leaderboard positions.
quote: Berkeley/RDI broke all 8 majors via reward hacking on April 12, 2026. Prefer third-party Epoch AI / BenchLM scores and run your own held-out eval.

claim: A two-dimensional taxonomy of agent evaluation organises work along evaluation objectives (behavior, capabilities, reliability, safety) and evaluation process (interaction modes, datasets, metrics, tooling).
quote: A survey provides a two-dimensional taxonomy organizing existing work along evaluation objectives (agent behavior, capabilities, reliability, safety) and evaluation process.

claim: DeepEval is an open-source (Apache 2.0) agent evaluation framework with 50+ metrics, CI-native pytest ergonomics.
quote: Largest open metric library (50+ scorers) with Apache 2.0 license

claim: Arize Phoenix provides OpenTelemetry-native auto-instrumentation across 14+ agent frameworks under open standards.
quote: Auto-instrumentation across 14+ agent frameworks under open specs

claim: OpenAI Evals is a YAML-defined MIT-licensed evaluation framework that runs anywhere CI runs, but lacks trajectory types and multi-agent rendering.
quote: YAML-defined, MIT licensed, runs anywhere CI runs. No trajectory type, no multi-agent rendering, not designed for agents.
